## Current signals

- WebNR remains a local-first browser reader and may be described as an independent browser-based alternative for some Legado users and web-first reading workflows. It is unaffiliated with Legado and is not an official Legado web client. Arbitrary Legado source JSON is not yet a drop-in WebNR runtime; compatibility claims remain tied to tested capability levels and versioned fixtures.
- Pull request #139 publishes the first-month source directory / health report and admits `CLiGS Textbox Spanish-American TXT Starter` as the 22nd maintained source family. The full health pass rechecked all 21 previously maintained families at their currently admitted capability boundary and found 21 retained, zero removals, zero downgrades, and zero failure-driven replacements.
- The CLiGS starter contains exactly three direct-TXT entries from `Collection of 19th Century Spanish-American Novels (1880-1916)`: `nh0003` / *Laucha*, `nh0004` / *Inca*, and `nh0011` / *Rumbo*. Every raw URL is pinned to upstream `cligs/textbox` commit `1b91e940475c8a7e866457a3953fed5edb0a29f1`; each selected file is below 1 MiB. The collection states that the authors' copyright has expired and publishes the collection under CC BY 4.0 with a citation request. WebNR preserves provenance/attribution and does not generalize that grant to unrelated CLiGS collections.
- CLiGS runtime behavior is bounded to one reader-initiated browser request for the selected commit-pinned raw TXT after the small WebNR source index is added. There is no background polling, catalog crawl, bulk clone, server proxy, credential/cookie use, account automation, JavaScript execution, archive extraction, or silent fallback to an unreviewed mirror.
- The 2026-09-03 new-candidate pass screened DBNL dataset, Project Laurens Jansz. Coster, Victorian Women Writers Project, Wright American Fiction 1851–1875, and Biblioteca Italiana. DBNL is the strongest next public-domain direct-TXT/TEI pilot candidate, but only an evidenced public-domain subset may be admitted. VWWP is a strong TEI candidate whose electronic-text header/attribution boundary must survive deterministic conversion. Wright and Biblioteca Italiana remain deferred until current stable endpoint/reuse-license and quality boundaries are sufficiently explicit. Coster should prefer a stable archival route because the legacy project is no longer updated.
- ELTeC and CoNSSA/TextGrid remain strong structured-text candidates but should enter only after deterministic TEI-to-reading-text fixtures preserve source identity, attribution, rights/version boundaries, unknown-node behavior, resource limits, and reproducible failure semantics. PleIAs Spanish-PD-Books remains a very large Parquet research corpus and is not treated as a reader catalog without a bounded indexed extraction path.
- Project Ben-Yehuda Public Domain TXT Starter remains a bounded four-entry direct UTF-8 source pinned to audited upstream public-domain dump commit `5e4277fead7b565f32cc4b352abd3565023a77d8`. GITenberg Direct TXT Starter remains a bounded three-entry Git-backed raw-TXT source. Folger Shakespeare TXT Starter remains a bounded three-entry first-party TXT source preserving Folger provenance and the CC BY-NC 3.0 attribution/noncommercial boundary. None of these catalogs is silently widened.
- Link-only is a proven current capability level rather than a permanent policy ceiling. Platform/community source families remain discovery-only unless a separate audit proves a richer API/feed/export boundary with stable identity, cadence, resource, attribution, update/deletion, and fixture semantics.
- `Fanfiction Discovery Starter` remains at eight audited first-party discovery destinations: FanFiction.Net, Fimfiction, Scribble Hub, Archive of Our Own (AO3), SquidgeWorld, fanfiction.lol, Sunset, and Asianfanfics. AO3 remains admitted for first-party Work Search discovery; canonical-tag Atom remains a richer machine-interface candidate requiring bounded transport, stable identity, update semantics, response/cadence limits, attribution, and versioned fixtures before synchronization is claimed.
- Fimfiction remains the strongest official-API upgrade candidate technically, but the current first-party developer/application-management path requires an externally created API application/client identity. WebNR must not fabricate credentials. Once that prerequisite exists, the adapter still requires bounded OAuth transport, rate-limit/backoff, caching, stable identity, cursor pagination, response/timeout bounds, provenance, attribution, update/deletion semantics, and fixtures.
- Pull request #126 remains the versioned Legado baseline: fixture suite `2026-08-30.1` and local-only inspector implement L1 import/inspection. L2 declarative, L3 stateful, L4 script, and L5 Bridge/WebView requirements may be recognized but are not executed. Inspection is bounded to 2 MiB and 500 source definitions and performs no target-site request, login, Cookie, JavaScript, WebView, CAPTCHA, paywall, robots, DRM, or access-control bypass.
- Pull request #127 remains the documentation analytics repair baseline. Reader and documentation output use only `G-DGH8HNQKE4`, require `page_location: window.location.href` and query-bearing `page_path: window.location.pathname + window.location.search`, and keep `allow_google_signals` plus `allow_ad_personalization_signals` false.
- `https://www.webnovel.win/` is the sole canonical public identity for documentation, reader-facing articles, search indexing, canonical tags, sitemap, and RSS. `https://app.webnovel.win/` is the reader application runtime; `https://autoarchive.github.io/webNR/` is an attributable documentation build mirror only.
